displayNumbers.label: DMG Bonus
displayNumbers.tooltip: The damage bonus is added to any damage done from Hand-to-Hand combat or CQC, which includes hand weapons such as knives, batons etc..

displayNumbers.label: Defense
displayNumbers.tooltip: Your defense is the base difficulty number to hit, that an attacker must equal or beat in order to be successful with a melee attack.

displayNumbers.label: Initiative
displayNumbers.tooltip: The initiative determines who goes when during combat; in the Battlefield section of the Active Operations Chapter (Pg 67), there are more in-depth rules on how the initiative is used in the game.

displayNumbers.label: Actions
displayNumbers.tooltip: Action points are also determined by the Focus and Reflex attribute. Operators receive 2 actions per turn, but this can increase the higher the attributes.

displayNumbers.label: ENC
displayNumbers.tooltip: Every operator will train with heavy packs meaning they start with the ability to act with a weight on their back. Encumbrance is done via a slot system, and this will include all the pockets, pouches, and packs the operator has at their disposal. A slot indicates both the weight and bulk of an object, with small objects taking up a half or full slot and more oversized items such as rifles taking up two slots.

displayNumbers.label: Perception
displayNumbers.tooltip: The operative’s ability to notice or sense danger and threats. Perception in Ghost Ops Second Strike is a passive ability rather than an active one. Threats must equal or beat the operator’s perception to launch a surprise attack or avoid discovery

poolResources.name: Boosts
poolResources.tooltip:
Each operator receives 3 Boosts these act similar to luck points in that they allow the player to change or effect results in the game. 
Boost Options
Re-Roll - The player can use a Boost to re-roll a fail on a challenge; they will have to accept the new roll.
Advantage - The player can use a Boost to give them an advantage (See Challenges Chapter for more on Advantages).
Aid - The player can use a Boost to aid another player; by spending a Boost, the player receives a +2.
Narrative - The player can affect the narrative by using a Boost, this can be done to make sure a door is unlocked, or a room is empty, the guard is asleep, or they have a flashback etc.. The Handler has the final say on how much of a change the player can make.
Disadvantage - A Boost can be used to give a Tango or even another Operator a Disadvantage (see challenges section for more on Disadvantages).
